questions.question: The epicentre of an earthquake is:
options: The point within the crust where the rupture begins
The point on the earth's surface directly above the focus
The deepest point reached by seismic waves
The centre of the earth

questions.question: Elastic rebound describes how:
options: Rock bends and stores strain energy until friction is overcome, then snaps back, releasing that energy as vibrations
Magma pushes the crust upward until it cracks
Ocean waves strike the coast and shake the land
The earth's magnetic field reverses and jolts the crust

questions.question: Shallow-focus earthquakes are the most destructive because:
options: They release more total energy than deep ones
They always occur in cities
The energy is released close to the surface, so less of it is absorbed before the shaking reaches buildings
They last much longer

questions.question: Most earth tremors felt in Gauteng and the Free State goldfields are:
options: Caused by the East African Rift
Aftershocks of the 1969 Ceres-Tulbagh earthquake
Volcanic in origin
Induced by deep mining rather than by plate tectonics

subtopics.title: Seismic Waves and Locating the Epicentre

questions.question: Which seismic wave arrives FIRST and can travel through solids, liquids and gases?
options: The P-wave (primary, compressional)
The S-wave (secondary, transverse)
The surface wave
They all arrive together

questions.question: Which wave causes MOST of the damage in an earthquake?
options: The P-wave, because it is fastest
The surface wave, because it has the largest amplitude and swings the ground furthest
The S-wave, because it cannot pass through liquid
None — damage is caused by the fault itself

questions.question: The time gap between the P-wave and S-wave arrivals at a station tells you:
options: The magnitude of the earthquake
The depth of the focus in kilometres
The DISTANCE from that station to the epicentre
The direction to the epicentre

questions.question: Three recording stations are needed to locate an epicentre because:
options: Each station measures a different wave type
Two stations always disagree
One station cannot record surface waves
One station gives only a distance — a circle of possible positions — and three circles intersect at a single point

subtopics.title: Richter and Mercalli — Two Different Measurements

questions.question: The Richter scale measures:
options: Magnitude — the energy released at the focus, giving one value per earthquake
Intensity — the damage observed at each place
The depth of the focus
The number of aftershocks

questions.question: Compared with a magnitude 5 earthquake, a magnitude 7 earthquake releases approximately:
options: Twice the energy
1 000 times the energy, with 100 times the ground movement
10 times the energy
100 times the energy, with 1 000 times the ground movement

questions.question: Why does one earthquake produce MANY Mercalli values?
options: Because different countries use different scales
Because the magnitude changes as the waves travel
Because intensity records observed effects, which vary with distance, ground conditions and building quality
Because Mercalli values are guesses

questions.question: Two towns the same distance from the epicentre record different Mercalli intensities. The most likely reason is:
options: The earthquake had two focuses
One town measured the P-wave and the other the S-wave
The Richter magnitude differed between them
One town is built on loose sediment that amplifies shaking, the other on solid bedrock

questions.question: Which of these is a SECONDARY effect of an earthquake?
options: Liquefaction, in which saturated loose sediment loses strength and buildings tilt and sink
Ground rupture along the fault line
The initial shaking of the ground
The release of energy at the focus

questions.question: A tsunami is generated when:
options: Strong winds blow across a warm ocean
An undersea earthquake displaces the sea bed vertically, lifting the whole water column above it
A volcano erupts on land near the coast
Two rivers meet at a delta

questions.question: The MAIN reason death tolls differ hugely between earthquakes of similar magnitude is:
options: Differences in the type of seismic wave produced
Differences in the time of year
Differences in vulnerability — building quality and enforcement, density, wealth, preparedness and ground conditions
Differences in the Richter scale used

questions.question: Base isolators fitted under a building work by:
options: Making the building heavier so it cannot move
Predicting the earthquake in advance
Absorbing the sound of the earthquake
Letting the ground move while the building above stays comparatively still

subtopics.title: Bending the Ruler Until It Goes

questions.question: In the bent-ruler comparison, the moment the ruler snaps represents:
options: The arrival of the surface wave
The focus — where the fault finally slips and stored energy is released
The epicentre on the surface
An aftershock

questions.question: If the rupture happens three kilometres beneath a soccer field, the epicentre is:
options: Three kilometres underground
Wherever the shaking is felt last
The middle of the soccer field, on the surface directly above the focus
At the nearest plate boundary

questions.question: Why are people kept out of damaged buildings after the main shock?
options: Because the Richter value has not yet been calculated
Because surface waves keep travelling for weeks
Because the epicentre may move
Because aftershocks continue for days or months and can finish off structures the main shock only cracked

subtopics.title: Thunder, Lightning and Three Friends with Phones

questions.question: The lightning-and-thunder comparison explains:
options: Why the gap between the P-wave and S-wave arrivals grows with distance from the epicentre
Why earthquakes happen during storms
Why deep earthquakes are less damaging
How the Richter scale is calculated

questions.question: An S-wave is best pictured as:
options: A bump running down a stretched spring
A ripple running along a flicked skipping rope — sideways shaking
A rolling swell along the ground surface
A sound wave in the air

questions.question: A station records a very SHORT gap between the P and S arrivals. This means the station is:
options: Far from the epicentre
On a different plate
Close to the epicentre
Recording only surface waves

questions.question: Triangulation locates an epicentre by:
options: Measuring the magnitude at three depths
Comparing Mercalli values in three towns
Timing three aftershocks
Drawing a distance circle around each of three stations and finding the single point where they intersect

subtopics.title: Two Ways to Score the Same Song — and Staying Alive

questions.question: In the stadium sound-system comparison, the Mercalli scale is like:
options: How loud it actually sounded where you were standing
The size of the amplifier at the source
The number of speakers used
The length of the concert

questions.question: Which statement about earthquake prediction is CORRECT?
options: Seismologists can name the exact date of the next major earthquake
High-risk zones and long-term probabilities can be identified, but no one can name a date, so preparedness matters more than prediction
Animal behaviour gives reliable warning a week ahead
Earthquakes cannot be studied at all before they happen

questions.question: The recommended personal action during strong shaking is:
options: Run outside immediately
Stand in an open doorway on the top floor
Drop, take cover under something solid, and hold on
Use the lift to reach ground level

questions.question: "Earthquakes do not kill people; falling buildings do" is used in the lesson to make the point that:
options: Shaking is harmless
Only tall buildings collapse
Magnitude does not matter at all
Deaths depend largely on construction quality, enforcement of codes, ground conditions and preparedness
